title: Sq'éwlets First Nation acquires Sasquatch Inn
content:
Published 10:26 am Monday, November 9, 2026

By Adam Louis

The Sq’éwlets First Nation has made a historic purchase.

Sq’éwlets Management Inc. recently completed the purchase of the Sasquatch Inn from the Maclean family, who has owned and operated the inn on traditional Sq’éwlets territory since 1954.

Sq’éwlets stated the Maclean family has always recognized and honoured the local history of the Indigenous people of the area with their connection to the Sq’éwlets people stretching back generations. When the time came for the next chapter for the Sasquatch Inn, the Macleans wanted to keep ownership local.

“The Sasquatch Inn has been part of life on the Harrison River, along Highway 7, for generations, and the Maclean family has been a good neighbour and a true friend to Sq’éwlets throughout that time,” said Sq’éwlets Chief Joseph Chapman (Hul-Lath-Tul). “We are honoured that the family entrusted this place to us. This is a step forward for our Nation’s economic independence, and it is also a story about relationships built over many years, rooted in respect for this land and the people who belong to it.”

The Sasquatch Inn is located at 46001 Lougheed Highway. It is a 12-room inn with a pub, restaurant and on-site liquor store. It has been a mainstay of the Lougheed Highway for more than 70 years and is a popular starting point for those visiting the Harrison River Valley.

Sq’éwlets intends to continue operating the inn, pub and liquor store under the Sasquatch Inn name and to retain the current staff. Sq’éwlets sees the purchase as a natural fit for their long-term economic development, tourism and Harrison River stewardship strategies.

“Our priority is continuity,” said Sq’éwlets Management Inc. CEO Colin Pennier. “Over time, we look forward to sharing more of Sq’éwlets’ story with the many visitors who stop here, in a way that reflects who we are as a Nation.”

The terms of the transaction have not been released.

The Sq’éwlets First Nation is located at the confluence of the Harrison and Fraser Rivers and is a member of the Stó:lō Tribal Council.

The Observer has attempted to reached out to the Maclean family for further comment.
